newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pacific BBA mulls selling Sarlon unit.
newsitem.headline: Pacific BBA mulls selling Sarlon unit.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific BBA Ltd said on Tuesday it would decide within the next six months whether or not it would sell or expand its industrial textiles business, Sarlon.
The company earlier said Sarlon dragged down its plastic division's earnings in the first half of 1997 and the business was now the subject of strategic review.

"Sarlon always loses money in the first half. It's seasonal. It makes all its money in the second half - we need to get volume through that facility or we will sell it to someone who can," Pacific BBA chief Barry Jackson told a media briefing.
Jackson said Pacific BBA was running out of patience with Sarlon but was not blaming the management, rather the tough market for its products and competition from imports.
"We'll fix it in the next six months one way or the other," he said.
Pacific BBA's Plastics division's sales fell five percent in the half while earnings before interest and tax dropped 42 percent.
The division's head, Trevor White said Sarlon had a negative impact of A$1.7 million on Plastics' earnings.
Pacific BBA earlier posted a 27 percent rise in net half profit to A$12.6 million for the six months to June 30.
